pains.title: Your real management software is a file nobody dares to touch.
items: Quotes, hours and inventory live in spreadsheets that contradict each other.
An Access database or in-house program runs the business, and the person who understood it has left.
Accounting runs in one app, operations in another — and someone copies from one to the other.
Every week, someone re-keys, checks and chases things by hand.
pains.cost: Double data entry, information nobody can find, forgotten follow-ups, errors, decisions made too late — and money left on the table.

method.title: How I work
method.sub: A small fixed-price step first. The rest only if the first one paid off.

steps.title: Free review
steps.text: We look at your spreadsheet, database or software and find the manual task that costs the most.

steps.title: First fixed-price sprint
steps.text: That task is automated or replaced, on your real data. From $4,500: one task eliminated, not a subscription.

steps.title: The rest of the system
steps.text: Replace the spreadsheet or old software piece by piece (in phases of about $6,000), or simply keep it running.

method.note: When artificial intelligence speeds up a step, it works on structured data, with guardrails and human approval. It’s a mechanism, not the product.

caps.title: Software gives you screens. A system does part of the work.
caps.sub: The system prepares, flags and follows up. Your people stay in control and make the calls.

services.title: What I do, concretely.

logiciel.title: Replace spreadsheets or Access
logiciel.text: Quotes, work orders, timesheets, inventory: real business software instead of files that contradict each other.

refonte.title: Take over existing software
refonte.text: An in-house program, an Access database or an old Windows app nobody maintains anymore: I take it over, stabilize it, then modernize it step by step.

automatisation.title: Automate a manual task
automatisation.text: The double entry, reports and follow-ups redone every week, handed to the machine.

documents.title: Invoices and documents read automatically
documents.text: Invoices, purchase orders, price lists: read, checked and entered without anyone re-typing them.

services.toolsLead: Your tools stay in place. The system replaces what no longer works and connects to what already does, depending on the access available.

proof.kicker: Case study: independent grocery store, Quebec
proof.txt: a year, recovered from a single manual task.

steps.label: The problem
steps.title: Re-typing thousands of prices, every week
steps.text: The team keyed their suppliers’ prices into the point-of-sale system by hand: the equivalent of a part-time job, not counting typing errors or the margin lost by ordering without comparing.

steps.label: The system
steps.title: The machine copies, the team approves
steps.text: It imports every supplier’s price list, compares prices product by product and prepares the update — connected to the existing point-of-sale system, without stopping operations.

steps.label: The result
steps.title: Time recovered, margin as a bonus
steps.text: Manual entry is gone, and the business now buys at the best price on every order.

me.quote: I don’t sell technology. I solve business problems.
me.body: Every project starts with how your operations really run — where time is lost, where information gets stuck, where money leaks out without anyone noticing — and ends with a system that does part of the work. No middlemen, no jargon, no surprises.
principles: Understand before building. We map your real operations and tools before proposing anything.
One point of contact. You talk to the person who analyzes your operations and builds the system.
Visible progress. The system is delivered in steps: you see each piece working before we go further.

for.title: Who it’s for
for.text: SMBs with 10 to 200 employees whose operations run on spreadsheets, Access or aging in-house software.
